title: Mutual Divorce: Can You Skip the 6-Month Wait?
desc: Section 13B lets courts waive the 6-month gap between motions in a mutual divorce if the couple has truly settled, including at Family Court Haldwani.
why: Courts across India, including a 2026 Andhra Pradesh High Court order, keep being asked to waive the statutory wait in mutual consent divorce, so the rule is worth explaining plainly.
keyPoints: Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 needs a first motion, then a second motion filed 6 to 18 months later.
The Supreme Court held in Amardeep Singh v Harveen Kaur (2017) that this 6-month gap is directory, not mandatory.
A court can waive the wait only if alimony, custody and other issues are genuinely settled and mediation has failed.
The waiver is never automatic — you must file a separate application asking the court to skip the gap.

sections.h: What is the waiting period in a mutual divorce?
p: A mutual consent divorce under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 needs two court appearances: a first motion, then a second motion filed 6 to 18 months later. In Haldwani, such petitions go to the Family Court. The gap exists so that a couple has time to reconsider before the marriage is finally dissolved.

Before filing the first motion, the couple must also show they have lived separately for at least one year and agree that the marriage has broken down. If either condition is missing, the petition itself cannot be filed as a mutual consent case.

sections.h: Can the court skip the 6-month wait?
p: Yes, in some cases. In Amardeep Singh v Harveen Kaur (2017) 8 SCC 746, the Supreme Court held that the 6-month period under Section 13B(2) is directory, not mandatory. A court may waive it only when it is satisfied that there is no chance of reconciliation and all disputes, including alimony, maintenance and custody of children, are already settled.

Courts still look case by case. In April 2026, an Andhra Pradesh High Court order upheld a waiver where a couple had resolved every issue, including alimony and child custody. This shows the test applies well beyond the Supreme Court, but it is still the court's discretion, not a right.

whatToDo: File the joint mutual consent petition (first motion) at the Family Court along with a written settlement on alimony, custody and property.
Attend any mediation or conciliation the court directs — a waiver is unlikely if reconciliation efforts have not been tried and failed.
If you want to skip the gap before the second motion, file a separate, written waiver application explaining that all issues are settled.
Keep proof of the settlement — maintenance amount, custody arrangement and any division of property — ready for the court.

hi.title: म्यूचुअल तलाक: क्या 6 महीने की अवधि माफ हो सकती है?
keyPoints: हिंदू विवाह अधिनियम, 1955 की धारा 13B के तहत पहले मोशन के बाद दूसरा मोशन 6 से 18 महीने बाद दाखिल होता है।
अमरदीप सिंह बनाम हरवीन कौर (2017) में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा कि यह 6 महीने की अवधि अनिवार्य नहीं है।
अदालत अवधि तभी माफ करती है जब गुजारा भत्ता, बच्चों की कस्टडी जैसे सभी मुद्दे सुलझ चुके हों और सुलह की कोशिश नाकाम रही हो।
अवधि माफी अपने आप नहीं मिलती — इसके लिए अलग से आवेदन देना पड़ता है।
